body_markdown:
Hey all,


A while back, we put together[Web Rewind](https://web-rewind.com/) to celebrate 30 years of the web, a site where you can travel through the internet’s past one era at a time. We’re happy to share that it has now won two gold w3 Awards, so it seems the jurors enjoyed it as much as we did.


## Two gold w3 Awards for Web Rewind


[Web Rewind](https://web-rewind.com/) has won gold in two categories:[General Websites – Marketing](https://www.w3award.com/winners/gallery/?event=1101&award=99&search=opera&id=398848) and[Campaigns – Integrated Campaign](https://www.w3award.com/winners/gallery/?event=1101&award=99&search=opera&id=398847) .


The w3 Awards, run by the Academy of Interactive and Visual Arts, reward excellence in digital content, design, and experiences. Entries are judged by the Academy’s members, a group of more than 500 people from institutions such as Microsoft, Netflix, and The Walt Disney Company, who score each work on a scale from one to ten. Gold generally goes to work that scores 9 or above, so both of our awards mean the jurors rated Web Rewind near the top of their scale.


## Take the trip yourself


These two awards join the[Red Dot: Best of the Best](https://blogs.opera.com/news/2026/11/opera-receives-a-red-dot-best-of-the-best-award/) we received for our work on agentic browsing, and the four[iF Design Awards](https://opr.as/xkos) from earlier this year. Thank you to the team who built Web Rewind, and to everyone who has taken a trip back through it with us.


If you haven’t been through it yet, you can find it at[web-rewind.com](https://web-rewind.com/) . For browsing the web as it is today, you can[download Opera here](https://www.opera.com/download) , and if you want to hear what we’re working on next, you can sign up for our newsletter at the bottom of this page.


Until next time!
